narr: A burst of monsoon moisture surged into eastern NM the morning of June 19th and surged through the gaps of the central mountain chain bringing high wind gusts of up to 58 miles per hour to parts of the Albuquerque metro that afternoon and evening. The strong east canyon wind during the evening resulted in a downed tree in the northeast heights of Albuquerque. The monsoon moisture surged through western NM and to the Arizona border by the morning of the 20th. The first event of flash flooding occurred on the 19th with thunderstorms developing along the east slopes of the central mountain chain. These slow moving storms dumped heavy rain in very localized and extremely sensitive areas of the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar from 2022 and within the most recent South Fork and Blue 2 burn scars near Ruidoso. Debris flows made roads impassable in the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn area and extremely inhibited fire recovery and response in the South Fork burn area. Large hail was also observed within both of these burn areas. Heavy rain acted to suppress the South Fork wildfire, but the cost was highly unjust for the benefits. Flash flooding was so bad that county emergency management issued an evacuation order for areas along the Rio Bonito and near Bonito Lake because of flash flooding within the Blue 2 burn area. A severe thunderstorm moving through the Albuquerque metro area also produced a localized dust storm that resulted in a 30 car accident along I-25 just north of Placitas. A slow moving storm over the Estancia Basin also dumped heavy rain, accumulating hail near the town of Willard. Flood waters and piles of hail resulted in stranded cars along highways near Willard, NM. The combination of flash flooding and severe weather continued into June 20th although prevailing high winds subsided in the Albuquerque metro area. Flash flooding was reported along the Rio Chama, Los Alamos and within the Hermit's Peak Calf/Canyon burn scar while a severe wind gust was observed at Gallup. A third day of flash flooding and severe weather struck on June 21st within the burn areas and Farmington. Debris flows were reported within the new South Fork burn area with more flash flooding within the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn area. Flash flooding was also reported along the Rio San Jose in Grants and in Farmington. The heavy rains over the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn area resulted in a flash flood emergency when flood waters overrode the Peterson Reservoir within the Gallinas Creek watershed just upstream of Las Vegas. An evacuation order was issued by city and county officials for residents along the Gallinas Creek and portions of Las Vegas, NM. Meanwhile, heavy rains occurring on June 20th within the Rio Chama basin resulted in a rise to just below Moderate flood stage near Chamita. While these flood waters subsided, major sand deposits near the village of Medanales resulted in the Rio Chama carving out a new path that pushed the flow of the river into adjacent agricultural areas. The threat of localized heavy rain continued on June 22nd, but there were no reports of impacts relayed as overall storm coverage waned into the weekend. More storms formed over the Sacramento Mountains midday June 23rd resulting in flash flooding and debris flows over the South Fork burn scar with the runoff allowing the Rio Ruidoso to instantly jump to a peak height of 11.43 feet. ||Key Words: Flash Flood, Debris Flow, Hail, Severe Wind Gust, River Flooding, Dust Storm.
ev: Heavy rains forced sharp rises along the Rio Chama between Medanales and Espanola. These rises were observed to peak at 7.95 feet at the Rio Chama near Chamita (CMTN5) gauge, resulting in flooding along U.S. Highway 84 between the junction of U.S. Highway 285 and Abiquiu that impacted 40 residences. This also resulted in heavy sand deposits near Medanales that resulted in the Rio Chama rerouting through adjacent agricultural fields two days later on June 22nd. Damage is an estimate given the lack of information and is an aggregate of the damage caused by the rerouting of the Rio Chama into the aforementioned agricultural fields as this was a direct result of the flash flooding that occurred on the night of the 20th into the morning of the 21st.

The Cibola County Emergency manager reported multiple vehicle rescues from flood waters. The Rio San Jose was out of its banks between Sargent and Davis Streets with several streets flooded in town. Swift moving water several inches deep was observed over First Street and Roosevelt Avenue. Damage is an estimate.

Heavy rain on the McBride burn scar resulted in flash flooding with mud and ash off the hillsides roughly between NM 48 and Eagle Creek Road, and a second area along Gavilan Canyon road by Meander Drive was washed out with debris over the roadway. Both sections of Gavilan Canyon Road were closed. A water main break also occurred that exacerbated the situation. Damage is an estimate based on clearing the debris on the roadway.

Heavy rains over the new South Fork burn scar resulted in flash flooding along Cedar Creek that raged through the Innsbrook Village near NM Highway 48. An NWS Employee also recorded flash flooding along Cedar Creek down to Paradise Canyon Drive. Damage is unknown, and may be more related to the South Fork Wildfire.

Flash flooding from heavy rains closed NM Highway 65 from mile markers 2 to 4 or one mile south of Montezuma where culverts were washed out. Flowing water 1 to 3 feet deep also reported over El Llano Road, Cinder Road, Palo Verde Road and at the intersection of 7th Street and Mills Avenue. Road closures were also reported along State Road 65 at Campus and El Camino, as well as along 8th Street north of Mills Avenue. Robertson Cardinal football field was completely covered in standing water. The Las Vegas Water Treatment Plant also flooded. A mandatory evacuation order was issued at 9:54pm MDT for this area due to the dangerous flooding across Las Vegas to Montezuma. Damage is an estimated given very limited information.

Broadcast media shared a report from a semi-truck driver of flash flooding along NM Highway 42 just southeast of Willard, NM. Accumulating hail and an estimated 6 to 8 inches of heavy rain washed out and shutdown this stretch of highway. Snow plows were needed to be used to clear the way. There are no reports of injuries or casualties. Damage is an estimate.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding along Eagle Creek and debris flow over State Highway 532.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding within the Blue 2 burn scar upstream of Bonito Lake.
NM State Emergency Operations Center relayed a report of flash flooding and mud slides along Gavilan Canyon Road within the McBride burn scar.

Emergency management relayed reports of swift water rescues out of the Rio Ruidoso near Hollywood and at the River Ranch RV Park along U.S. Highway 70. Emergency management requested a flash flood emergency be issued along the Rio Ruidoso down to the Two Rivers Dam. There was an unknown number of people rescued.
Underpass to I-25 Exit 361 flooded with rapidly rushing water and widespread flooding in the fields along the interstate. That road was covered with several inches of small hail.
NM 542 just north of the intersection with NM 55 closed due to heavy rains and 8 to 10 inches of fast flowing water over the highway.

Multiple reports of flash flooding across Farmington including along the La Plata and San Juan Rivers, including vehicles driving across flooded low water crossings. A video from the emergency manager showed the La Plata River raging and partly out of its banks. These included along Southside River Road on the west side of Farmington. A vehicle was stuck in a ditch along the San Juan River, thankfully the driver made it out safely. There was an overflowing ditch and arroyo with fast moving water at Brookside Drive and Navajo Street. There was several inches of water moving across Crouch Mesa east of Farmington and south of Flora Vista. U.S. Highway 64 at Andrea Drive and between County Road 5500 and 5777 where the road was completely flooded with swift moving water and impassable. A normally dry wash also observed a one foot rise with debris including small pieces of furniture. Flooding lasted well after the heavy rains ended as evident on the San Juan River gauge (FRMN5) showing river levels did not recede until after 10:00 pm MDT. Damage is an estimate based on the very limited information provided.
Widespread flooding reported along Tecolote Creek in Mineral Hill stretching over to NM Highway 283 from mile markers 3 to 13 that closed the highway. Any damage is unknown.

Flash flooding and debris flow within the eastern edge of the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar resulted in a bridge being washed out along County Road A3. Exact location is unknown and damage is an estimate.

Flooding over U.S. Highway 85 at mile markers 200 and 204 requiring debris removal. Reports of home damage from arroyo flooding, and a water rescue of a couple trapped in a mobile home due to surrounding flood waters. Injuries are unknown. Flood damage reported in homes from the arroyo flooding. Damage costs are an estimate.

Raging waters on Cedar Creek overtopped its banks in spots, resulting in the closure of Paradise Canyon Road near Hull Road. Muskat Ball Drive at Cedar Creek was impassable due to flooding with medium to heavy debris. County Road 127A (Upper Eagle Creek Road) was impassible with medium to heavy debris along the road. Alto Lake also flooded over a short time.
